_note: Every published video is tagged with these attributes BEFORE publishing. The learning loop can only learn about attributes that are recorded. Add new values here first, never invent them ad hoc.

postmortems.promise: How one mistake broke a big system, in 40 seconds

security.promise: How it's exploited, how it's fixed

databases.promise: What your database does when you hit enter

networking.promise: What really travels between client and server

browser.promise: What the browser does with your code

systems.promise: Popular tools, explained from the inside

vpn.promise: VPN and privacy mechanics, no marketing

series._note: Series names are placeholders until the channel name is chosen. A recurring format helps viewers know what to expect and follow.

system-design.promise: How big systems are built, one idea at a time

hook_type.question: Opens with a question the viewer wants answered
hook_type.bold_claim: Opens with a surprising statement that the video then proves
hook_type.number: Opens with a concrete number or quantity (must be verified)
hook_type.story: Opens as a short story of an event
hook_type.myth_bust: Opens by attacking a common belief
hook_type.mystery: Opens with an unexplained effect, answer comes later
hook_type.mistake: Opens with a mistake the viewer may be making
hook_type.howto: Opens with a promise to explain a process step by step

derived_fields.hook_words: word count of the hook text
derived_fields.hook_has_number: true if the hook contains a digit
derived_fields.hook_is_question: true if the hook ends with a question mark
derived_fields.weekday: 0-6 from published_at in the audience time zone

_controlled_note: During the explore phase these stay fixed so that differences come from topic and hook, not from five things changing at once.
_visual_note: visual is a descriptive tag; render uses only existing scene types (diagram, code, checklist, browser). Add a new scene type in src/scenes/ only when a topic truly needs it.
